### Summary

items.title: dd-trace: ReDOS in URL query string obfuscation
items.description:
### Summary

A regular expression used to obfuscate URL query strings can consume excessive CPU when processing certain attacker-controlled input. This can stall request processing and cause denial of service in applications using affected HTTP tracing integrations.

### Details

The default query-string obfuscation pattern can exhibit excessive backtracking. The pattern is applied synchronously when recording HTTP URL metadata, allowing query-string processing to occupy application resources for an extended period.

As a workaround, set DD_TRACE_OBFUSCATION_QUERY_STRING_REGEXP to the fixed regex below, then restart the application.

```
DD_TRACE_OBFUSCATION_QUERY_STRING_REGEXP='(?:(?:"|%22)?)(?:(?:old[-_]?|new[-_]?)?p(?:ass)?w(?:or)?d(?:1|2)?|pass(?:[-_]?phrase)?|secret|(?:api[-_]?|private[-_]?|public[-_]?|access[-_]?|secret[-_]?|app(?:lication)?[-_]?)key(?:[-_]?id)?|token|consumer[-_]?

items.title: TinyMCE Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability using media plugin `data-mce-object` serialization
items.description:
### Impact
Stored XSS vulnerability in the media plugin. Attackers can inject malicious scripts via elements crafted through the data-mce-object attribute, which are created and executed before sanitization. Impacts users of TinyMCE with the media plugin enabled.

### Patches
This vulnerability has been patched in TinyMCE 8.9.3 and TinyMCE 7.9.4 by ensuring that, when using the media plugin, any content created through the data-mce-object attribute is properly sanitized first.

### Workarounds
No official workaround available.

### Fix
To avoid this vulnerability:

Upgrade to TinyMCE 8.9.3 or higher.
Upgrade to TinyMCE 7.9.4 or higher.

### Acknowledgements
Tiny thanks [Fariskhi Vidyan](https://github.com/farisv) and David Vieira Kurz (HiSolutions AG) for their help identifying this vulnerability.

items.description:

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability has been discovered in the CKEditor 5 engine. This vulnerability could be triggered by inserting specially crafted markup under a specific General HTML Support configuration that allows inserting objects, leading to unauthorized JavaScript code execution in a browser context isolated from the origin of the application embedding the editor.

This vulnerability affects only installations where General HTML Support is enabled and configured to allow the affected HTML content.

The problem has been recognized and patched. The fix will be available in version `48.5.1` (and above) and `47.7.4` (LTS).

CTFer.io's CTFd Terraform Provider stores `ctfd_team.password` as non-sensitive values (CWE-522). A local or remote attacker, who can have access to the Terraform state, can read team passwords without the need for the state password for decryption.

items.description:
In rustls 0.23.44 and 0.23.45, application data that a client buffers before the handshake completes is sent to the server even when the server rejects Encrypted Client Hello (ECH).

When the server rejects ECH, the client completes the handshake with the outer ClientHello and authenticates the server against the ECH config's `public_name`. The application then receives `Error::PeerIncompatible(ServerRejectedEncryptedClientHello)`, as expected. However, the client is still expected to call `write_tls()` to send the fatal alert, and that call also sends the encrypted application data. The server decrypts the data and only then receives the alert.

The built-in (but disabled by default) Brotli certificate decoder bounds the output buffer but accepts an input-selected history window. A header of five bytes can specify a 1 GiB window allocation. items.description:
### Summary

Authlib's RFC 9101 (JAR) extension passes the attacker-controlled `request_uri` authorization parameter straight to the `get_request_object()` fetch hook with no validation, at a pre-authentication endpoint. `OctKey.import_key()` carries the only guard that stops an asymmetric public key from being used as an
HMAC secret in `authlib.jose`. That guard is `raw_key.startswith(POSSIBLE_UNSAFE_KEYS)` — anchored at

issuer's public key then mints an `HS256` token with arbitrary claims that `jwt.decode()` accepts as
authentic.

items.description:
### Impact
`Snappy.uncompressCharArray`, `uncompressShortArray`, `uncompressIntArray`, `uncompressLongArray`, `uncompressFloatArray` and `uncompressDoubleArray` sized the result array by dividing the declared uncompressed byte length by the element size, but native code wrote the full byte length. If the declared length is not a multiple of the element size, up to 7 bytes are written past the end of the Java array, corrupting the heap.

### Patches
Fixed in 1.1.10.9 ([#739](https://github.com/xerial/snappy-java/pull/739)). These methods now reject uncompressed lengths that are not a multiple of the element size with `SnappyIOException`.

### Workarounds
Check that `Snappy.uncompressedLength(input)` is a multiple of the element size before calling these methods.

Fixed in 1.1.10.9 (#741). `Snappy.arrayCopy` checks both ranges before copying. The stream `read`/`write` methods validate offsets and lengths, and reject typed-array ranges whose byte size overflows `int`.

### Workarounds
Validate offsets and lengths before calling these methods.

items.title: Pylint: Arbitrary code execution via pickle deserialization of the stats cache in PYLINT_HOME
items.description:
### Impact

Since 2006 / pylint 0.15.2, pylint caches its stats as pickles in `PYLINT_HOME` and reload them on the next run with `pickle.load`. Someone without access to the configuration or linted code, but with access to the cache directory (predictable `PYLINT_HOME` on a multi-user host) can write a crafted pickle that will runs arbitrary code when pylint access its stat cache.

### Patches

From pylint 4.0.9, the result cache is now stored as JSON instead of pickle, preventing code-execution. 

### Workarounds

Until upgrading do not point `PYLINT_HOME` to an untrusted, shared, or group-writable directory. The default value, `~/.cache/pylint`, is writable only by the user running pylint.

### Credits

- Reported privately via Tidelift coordinated disclosure (Dan Lenz).
